pr_title: Assign indices of PIT requests in transport layer
pr_body:
- Reject search requests that have both indices and point-in-time
- Assign the indices of PIT requests in the transport layer; otherwise, the indices of internal requests aren't assigned correctly

Closes #84187
pr_comments: Hi @dnhatn, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
Hi @dnhatn, I've updated the changelog YAML for you.

@javanna @ywangd 

>  Possibly an alternative hack: would it work to make what SearchReqest#indices return dynamic and extract the indices from pit if a pit is set?

While working on this proposal, I found it's fragile. We need to carefully set and unset the point-in-time when updating the indices. Below is one of our usages that can be an issue. If we don't unset the `point-in-time` before retrieving `indices()` then we can add extra index filters to the search request although the actual indices can be empty.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/273eeddc14601988ad0a70f0b199d163c6e09f1d/x-pack/plugin/eql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/eql/execution/search/PITAwareQueryClient.java#L105-L110

> Though I'd rather add the new base method to ActionRequestinstead of TransportAction because calling ActionRequest#validate() and ActionRequest#prepare() in sequence seems to be more fluent to me (it would be nice to make ActionRequest#prepare idempotent).

Now I think we should go with Yang's proposal.

> While working on this proposal, I found it's fragile. We need to carefully set and unset the point-in-time when updating the indices.

IIUC, the issue is that changing `point-in-time` for a `SearchRequest` also leads to change of the output from `SearchRequest.indices()`. This interaction could be unexpected and depending on the order of calls, the resulted `indices` can be different. If you want to use the `indices` subsequently in other places, it might not do what you meant to do.

If we could prevent setting `pointInTimeBuilder` when the `SearchRequest` has non-empty `indices`, would that help? In theory, it makes sense to prevent it from happening since we are already preventing it at the REST (API) layer. That said, I am aware it might be technically challenging since `SearchSourceBuider` does _not_ know about `SearchRequest`?

Nhat and I have discussed this and I was hoping that we could find a simpler, less intrusive solution for this problem. Given that the transport client is no longer around, we should not design our system for direct access to the transport layer, hence I would opt for adapting the search request setup on the client side to set the indices in addition to the point in time.
We decided not to proceed with this change, closing.

issue_context.title: Move point in time setup to the transport layer?
issue_context.body:
Some parts of the point in time setup happen on the REST layer, see https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/13390dd4d820834a4b0135bfb5d24618accb15f2/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/rest/action/search/RestSearchAction.java#L373-L374 . This causes problems to consumers that call search directly at the transport layer. Either those consumers reploicate the same setup on their side before calling search, or that setup is shared and moved from the REST layer to `TransportSearchAction`?

In practice, this ends up causing EQL to hit all indices when using point in time, instead of the configured indices.
comments: @dnhatn do you have opinions on how to proceed? The description of the issue includes two options, but maybe there are other ways.
Good find. Thanks @ywangd and @javanna. I've opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/84202.
We decided not to proceed with this change, see https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/84202#issuecomment-1072547030.
